description: Renovate raises what Dependabot cannot read: mise.toml, the mise version pins and the integration's runtime requirements. Inert without the Renovate GitHub App.
manifest.json is bumped together with requirements.txt, so one package lands in one pull request; a workflow input is named by a `# renovate:` comment directly above it.
script/template-sync-guard reads the managers and patterns here to know which pins a template sync must not lower.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Needs Dependabot alerts on in the repository settings. Users only receive a fixed version with a new release.

packageRules.description: Dependabot's share (.github/dependabot.yml). To let Renovate raise these instead, delete that file together with this rule and the next one; the tooling rules below already group them.
Runtime: what Home Assistant installs for users. One pull request per package; a routine bump stays `chore`, only a security fix is worth a release of its own.
A runtime major waits on the dependency dashboard for a person.
Tooling: everything that runs the checks, CI and the editor moves in one grouped pull request a week; a major update gets one of its own.
A new action version settles a week before it runs with the repository's token, as in Home Assistant Core.
Home Assistant decides the Python version. Raise it by hand together with the Home Assistant version.
Renovate's own engines refuse a Node major newer than this.

Each release tracks one Home Assistant version. A new release train means raising the minimum in hacs.json, which script/ha-version-sync enforces; a pre-release dependency is closed by the HA stability check workflow.

The secret scanners carry their detection rules in the binary, so a release is mostly new rules: outside the weekly schedule, still after the release age, and merged once the pull request's checks are green. A release that finds something keeps them red and the pull request open.
